claims.text: The as-synthesized high-entropy alloy has maximal atomic-scale chemical or configurational disorder.
Controlled annealing can partially increase local chemical order in the selected alloy.
The relevant superconducting test regime is below approximately 10 K.
Local chemical ordering reduces randomness in atomic-site occupation.
Partial local ordering improves matching between electronic states and lattice vibrations.
Partial local ordering enhances electron-phonon coupling.
Stronger electron-phonon coupling promotes Cooper pairing and can raise the superconducting transition temperature.
Greater disorder can suppress superconductivity, and increasing mixing entropy has been observed alongside decreasing Tc in superconducting high-entropy alloys.
Annealed samples with increased local order will have a higher Tc than the as-synthesized baseline.
Annealed samples will have a narrower, sharper superconducting transition than the as-synthesized baseline.
The proposed ordering effect should hold only when annealing does not cause phase separation.
The proposed ordering effect should hold only when annealing does not cause large-scale grain growth or a crystallographic phase change.
Impurity-phase formation could obscure the expected relationship between local ordering and Tc.
The annealed and as-synthesized samples will be compared while other synthesis parameters are held constant.
Electrical resistivity and magnetic susceptibility will be used to identify the superconducting transition.
Failure of verified local ordering to produce a statistically significant Tc increase or transition sharpening relative to the baseline would falsify the hypothesis.
